steps_h2: How to Make a Product Launch Video in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: A Facebook promo video starts with one photo of the finished item, a short reveal line, and a file you can post.

steps.d: Use one clear photo of the finished item you plan to release. Keep the whole product inside the frame.
Name a reveal, an unboxing, or a short demo. Then pick 9:16 or 1:1 and a length from 6 to 30 seconds.
Download the file and add the release date and offer in your editor. Do not promise a date you have not set.

faq.q: What is a product launch video?
faq.a: It is a new product promo video for the day you release a finished item. Add a script, a voice, captions, and an AI actor if you want a presenter.

faq.q: How do I make the launch clip?
faq.a: Upload a photo of the finished item, name the reveal, and pick a size and a length. Lengths are 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.

faq.q: Why start from a photo instead of a launch shoot?
faq.a: You can cut the reveal before release day without booking a creator. Check that the item on screen matches the finished product.
Shops and agencies announcing a finished item on Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube. A first file does not require an editing background.

faq.q: Can I do this on the first try?
faq.a: Yes. Use one clear photo, describe a reveal or an unboxing, and download the file. Add the confirmed date in your editor if captions should not carry it.
One clear photo of the finished item, with the whole product in frame. A product page link works when you want a first draft from the listing.

faq.q: How is a teaser different from release day?
faq.a: A teaser can say the item is coming. On release day, add only a date and an offer you have confirmed. Do not let the script invent either one.

faq.q: Which size and length can I pick?
faq.a: Use 9:16 or 1:1 for this launch clip. Other sizes are 16:9, 4:3, and 3:4. Lengths are 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.

A video is 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, and 120 for 30. Starter is $24.50 a month with 200 credits. You see the cost before the job starts, and a failed job returns those credits. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: Can I publish it to TikTok or Meta?
faq.a: Yes. Publish to TikTok, Instagram, or Facebook in one step, or download a file for YouTube. You can use it in ads. People on screen are AI actors.

faq.q: Can I announce several items at once?
faq.a: Yes. Run the same reveal across a batch of photos, or send the catalog through the API. Each job shows its credit cost first.
